idea-plugin.name: Duo Watchdog
idea-plugin.description:
Keep an eye on your GitLab Duo credits without leaving the IDE.

Duo Watchdog tracks your own GitLab Credits for the current billing period, forecasts where the month will end, and warns you before you hit your limit.

What you get

  • A meter in the status bar: credits used out of your limit, amber from your first threshold, red when GitLab blocks you. A click opens the dashboard.
  • A dashboard: used, left, the month-end forecast, your pace and what you spent today, with usage by day and by feature.
  • Alerts, once a billing period: when the forecast passes your limit, at each threshold you set (80% and 95% unless you change them), at the limit, and when GitLab blocks you.
  • Statistics: the last 3, 6 or 12 months, by feature.
  • Sessions: your Duo Agent Platform sessions and an estimate of what each cost, with the Duo CLI session in progress live in the status bar.
  • Duo CLI quick actions: New Session, Doctor and quick commands of your own, in a terminal in the project.
  • Several accounts: one token for each, on gitlab.com or a GitLab of your own, rotated a week before it expires.
  • Updates from the IDE: an Update button on this page when a newer release is out, and Tools | Duo Watchdog: Check for Updates…

Getting started

  1. Open Settings | Tools | Duo Watchdog and click + (Add Token…).
  2. Paste a personal access token with the scopes read_api and ai_features; GitLab says whose it is.
  3. Set your limit. The Duo Watchdog tool window on the right shows the rest.

Needs GitLab 19.4 or later, and membership of the group that owns the GitLab Duo subscription; the Owner role is not required. The token is kept in the IDE's password store.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
What's new in 0.7.2

  • The IDE itself offers each new release: Update on Duo Watchdog's page in Settings | Plugins, with the versions (0.7.2 → 0.7.3), as for a plugin from the Marketplace. Duo Watchdog adds its releases on GitHub to the IDE's plugin repositories; turning Check for Duo Watchdog updates off in its settings takes them out again.
  • This page says what the plugin does and how to start, with a Plugin homepage link.

0.7.1

  • The installers download the ready-made plugin of the latest release from GitHub and check it against the release; nothing is built.
  • Every release is built and checked by GitHub Actions, with JetBrains' Plugin Verifier, before it is published.

0.7.0

  • Updates from the IDE: Duo Watchdog asks GitHub for its latest release when the IDE starts and then once a day, and says when a newer one is out. Update downloads its plugin zip from GitHub, checks it against the release, and the IDE puts it in place when it restarts (Restart Now). The tool window's toolbar shows Update to x.y.z while one is known; Tools | Duo Watchdog: Check for Updates asks at once. Settings | Updates turns the daily check off.
  • The Duo CLI's tool approval reads Manual or Auto (--dangerously-skip-permissions).
  • Sessions' By project puts each project on a line of its own over its bar, cut from the front so its own name shows, with the whole path on hover.

0.6.0

  • Duo CLI quick actions on Usage: a row under the toolbar with two drop-downs, duo or glab duo cli, and Ask before tools or Auto-approve tools (--dangerously-skip-permissions), then New Session, Doctor and your quick commands. Each runs the CLI in a new Terminal tab in the project; Doctor then types /doctor at its prompt, and a quick command its own, such as /ab-testing. + builds one: the command first, then its button's name (AB Testing); Settings lists them to change, move or remove. A command is typed only once the CLI has started a log of its own.

0.5.3

  • Every time shown says its day and its zone, on this computer's clock: Updated today 11:45 UTC+2, and the Duo CLI session's Started today 10:00 UTC+2, 34m 17s, quiet since today 10:34 UTC+2, with yesterday or the date for an older one.

0.5.2

  • The Duo CLI session in the status bar always shows its ≈ $: a step on the group's default model, on a model the log does not name, or on one with no known rate is priced as the Group default model set in Settings (Sonnet 4.5 unless you pick another). The tooltip and the Sessions tab say which model it takes.

0.5.1

  • The session of the interactive Duo CLI (9.30) counts its round trips, one per prompt, and shows even before its first tool call.
  • A session on the group's default model says Group default.
  • A project in WSL has its Duo CLI runs followed once, not twice.

0.5.0

  • The Duo CLI session, live: while duo runs a session, a small status bar item beside the credits shows how long it has run, its round trips (prompts sent), steps (model calls) and ≈ credits, each step at its model's credits per call, updated within seconds of each step. Its mini meter fills toward the round trips recommended per session (20 unless set in Settings), amber from 80% and red at it. The Sessions tab starts with the same session. Read from the CLI's own log; tokens are not shown, since GitLab bills per model call.
  • Token rotation: a week before a token expires, GitLab replaces it with a new one that lives as long, saved and handed to glab; the notice copies it for wherever else you use it. On by default. The Token saved box says when the token rotates, or why it won't.
  • Released under the MIT License.

0.4.0

  • Several accounts, one token each. An account is one GitLab user on one GitLab: when you add a token, GitLab says whose it is, and a token for an account already listed replaces its token, keeping its group and limit. Each account has its own group path and limit.
  • Accounts in Settings: credits left, the token and its expiry date for each, most credits left first, with All / Has credits / Expired filters and a search. A saved token shows as dots in a locked field, a missing one as an empty field; the token itself is never shown.
  • Add Token says what OK will do: add an account, replace a token, or add an account whose usage can't be tracked (no ai_features scope), instead of failing.
  • The tool window has an account switcher; the status bar follows it, with a dot when another account needs a look, and its tooltip lists every account.
  • Popups that stay until closed: the last alert threshold, the limit or a block, a token that expires within 3 days, and a token GitLab turns down.
  • glab and the GitLab Duo CLI: an account can hand its token to glab, and so to the Duo CLI. Both are off unless you tick them.
  • A Statistics tab next to the dashboard: the last 3, 6 or 12 months by month and by feature, with what GitLab did not bill, for one account or all of them.
  • A Sessions tab: your Agent Platform sessions over the days you pick, each with its credits estimated from the day's credits per feature and, where the Duo CLI's logs on this machine count them, the agent's steps. Look a session up by its ID or link, or show the last one.
  • What's New: after an update a window shows what the version brings, with pictures; Help | What's New in Duo Watchdog opens it again.
  • The token saved by 0.3.0 moves to its account on the first refresh, with its group, limit and last alert.

0.3.0

  • Spent today: a new tile on the dashboard, and a line in the status bar tooltip.
  • Token status in Settings: green with a check mark when a token is saved, amber when there is none or it expires within a week, red when GitLab turns it down. It says when the token was saved, when it expires and which scopes it has.
  • Check connection asks GitLab whose the token is, when it expires, and for your group's credits.
  • Find my group says what it does, and the token now comes before the group, since Find my group asks GitLab with it.
  • Shift+Esc hides the Duo Watchdog tool window and Esc goes back to the editor, as in the IDE's own tool windows.
  • The installers: choose IntelliJ IDEA, VS Code or both with the arrow keys, and follow the install on a progress bar.
